headline: On the engine-architecture lens, v5.0 is **not** smarter than what we shipped — it is a less-complete version of our own architecture, described in different words, with invented numbers where we have 279 citations. Its central premise ("100 brisket recipes are 95 combinations of the same variables") is already how our data is built: `data.py` stores 130 cuts as a **parameter record** (svt/svh/smt/smh/sot/soh/tgt/safe/wrap/mid/sear/rest/…), and `itemProfile`/`validCombo`/`methodRules`/`comboMethodEntry`/`itemStages` already **generate** every stage and every method-combo from those parameters. But three of its mechanisms are genuinely new to us and worth taking: per-stage **transition predicates** (advance-on-core-temp, not just a duration), an explicit **gain/loss vector** on each path, and a **consumables** model. The infrastructure half is a split verdict: a Worker/Supabase tier is the only way to ingest IoT telemetry and is worth building for **user/event data** — but moving the rules engine or the safety values server-side must be refused outright.
isItSmarter:
**Worse, on the two things that matter most on this lens: generation-of-values, and failure modes.**

**1. Generation vs derivation.** The proposal (§1.1): *"אם תאסוף 100 מתכונים לעישון בריסקט, 95 מהם הם קומבינציות שונות של אותם משתנים בדיוק… לבנות 'מתכון-על' (Master Recipe) מבוסס משתנים."* We already did that — and the measurement refutes the premise at the value level. Across our 130 cuts, the tuple `(svt, svh, smt, smh, tgt, safe)` has **116 distinct values out of 130 (89%)**. The *variables* are shared (that is the Master Recipe idea, and we have it); the *numbers* are per-recipe cited fact. What v5.0's engine actually generates in `§4.5` is the opposite: `if (SOUS_VIDE && collagen_level === "HIGH") → chamber_temp: "68°C", duration: "24_HOURS"` — **two constants** standing in for 116 distinct cited schedules. Our brisket is `svt 68 / svh 30`, beef cheek `80/24`, oxtail `79/24-48`, beef tongue `70/24-48`, octopus `77/5h`. Adopting the generic engine would not shorten our recipes; it would delete the cited content and replace it with a guess. That is data loss dressed as a refactor.

**2. Failure modes.** `generateRecipePipeline` **throws** — `throw new Error("חסימת מערכת: נתח עשיר בקולגן דורש בישול ארוך. אין ציוד מתאים.")`. Our `eqmValidity(meta)` (app.js:1859) returns `{level: 'ok'|'blocked-default'|'uncookable', okPaths, gaps, fixes}`. The `blocked-default` level exists precisely so we do not "cry wolf on an item the user can in fact cook another cited way" (comment at app.js:1846) — the default combo is blocked but another cited path works, so the item is still addable (`eqmAddGate` blocks on `uncookable` only, app.js:2059). And `fixes` names the remedy: configure the device, or *"זמין במסלול: X"* — switch to the specific cited path that works. v5.0 has no equivalent of `blocked-default`, no `fixes`, no path enumeration. It throws a string for the most fixable class of problem there is (missing equipment). This is not a close call: our model is better for the user, and better as code.

**3. Its own code does not implement its own rules.** §4.1 declares 7 hard rules. §4.5's `generateRecipePipeline` implements ~1.5 of them: Rule 1 partially (recast as an *equipment* check, not a method check), Rule 5 weakened to a warning with the 30°C threshold dropped entirely, Rule 6 partially (skin scoring, but the promised `ADD_STAGE_TO_END("PAN_SEAR_HIGH_HEAT")` is absent). Rules 2 (poultry pasteurization), 3 (sugar burn), 4 (fish), 7 (pork) appear nowhere in the code. `flavor.has_sugar` is declared in the interface and never read. `P_TARGET_INT`, `P_MOIST_ENV`, `P_TIME_LIMIT`, `P_FINISH` from the §3.1 parameter table never appear.

**4. Its flagship example is unreachable by its own engine.** §3.2's headline pipeline is `["STAGE_1_SMOKE", "STAGE_2_SOUS_VIDE", "STAGE_3_GRILL_FINISH"]`. In §4.5 the sous-vide branch and the smoker branch are `if (…SOUS_VIDE && HIGH) {…} else if (hasSmoker) {…}` — **mutually exclusive**. The engine can never emit smoke+sous-vide in one pipeline. We ship both orders, and gate the reverse one on cited data: `comboHasSvSmoke` (app.js:4216) returns true only when `order_smokesv.sv.pasteurize === true` — *"No cited data → sv→smoke only; never a generic svHours>=1 guess."*

**Where it is genuinely ahead:** stage **transition predicates**. §3.2 writes `TRIGGER_NEXT_STAGE_WHEN = (TIME_ELAPSED == 2_HOURS) OR (P_TARGET_INT == 50°C)`. Our `itemStages` stages carry `{label, hours, kind, temp, note}` — a **duration only**. We have exactly one internal-temp gate, the terminal `bcheck` (D1). A stage that advances on core temperature is a real modelling capability we do not have, and it is the correct shape for a live cook. That is the one place the proposal is architecturally smarter than us.

adopt.item: Per-stage transition predicate — add an `advanceWhen` field to the stage object emitted by `itemStages`, e.g. `{tempC: 71}` / `{elapsedH: 2}` / `{either: [...]}`, populated ONLY from cited data (never a formula), defaulting to today's pure-duration behaviour when absent.
adopt.why: This is the one genuinely new idea in the proposal (§3.2 `TRIGGER_NEXT_STAGE_WHEN`). Our stages carry `hours` and nothing else; the only internal-temp gate we have is the terminal `bcheck` appended by `itemStages` (app.js:4170, D1). A wrap stage that fires "when the core hits 71°C" is physically correct — the stall is an evaporative plateau at an internal temperature — whereas a clock is an approximation. It is also the missing input for Phase 3b live Copilot: today the Copilot has a probe reading and no stage-level predicate to test it against.
adopt.whereItPlugsIn: `itemStages()` (app.js:4093–4169) — the single stage authority; add the field, never change an existing one. `deriveRequires()` (equipment.js:63) already reads the stage array and would naturally tag `capability.probe` on any stage carrying a `tempC` predicate, exactly as it does today for `bcheck` (the O-7 amendment). Consumers: `planSchedule` (app.js:3846) keeps using `hours` as the scheduling estimate; the work-plan stage row (app.js:7421) renders the predicate as a second line. Data source: `sources.py` — `order_svsmoke`/`order_smokesv` already carry per-stage `{t, h}`; the predicate is a third key on the same cited object.

adopt.item: Fix the `grillable` inconsistency we found: `sources.py` carries a **cited per-cut boolean** `grillable` (25 of 130 are `False`, each with its own `src.grill` note, e.g. brisket: *"לא לגריל ישיר: נתח קולגני עבה…"*) — but `methodRules()` gates grill combos on a **category heuristic** (`isProduce`/`isOffal`/`c.doneness`) and never reads it. `grillable` is display-only (app.js:2823, 2896).
adopt.why: Not a v5.0 idea, but the proposal's §4.1 Rule 1 ("chewiness protection") is exactly this rule, and comparing the two surfaced that our cited flag is orphaned while a heuristic decides. Under our own rules the citation should be the authority. `itemPaths` currently stamps `cited:true` on every enumerated combo unconditionally (app.js:4180) — so a combo the citation argues against is still labelled cited. This is a correctness gap in the layer the whole equipment engine converges on.
adopt.whereItPlugsIn: `methodRules(c)` / `validCombo(c, combo)` (app.js:990–1048) — add `grillable===false` to the `needsCookFor:'grill'` / `invalid` construction so the cited flag narrows the enumeration; `itemPaths` (app.js:4175) then stops emitting an uncited-by-its-own-source path. Cascades cleanly into `eqmValidity` (fewer false `okPaths`) with no data change.

adapt.item: Method-conversion / path comparison with an explicit attribute gain-loss vector — §4.4's `SET LOSS_OF_ATTR = ["BARK", "SMOKE_AROMA"]` / `SET GAIN_OF_ATTR = ["HIGHER_JUICINESS"]`.
adapt.why: The *shape* is good and we have nothing like it. `itemPaths` returns `{id, methodKey, order, label, cited, isDefault}` — a label and no consequence. A user choosing between sv→smoke and smoke→sv today gets no statement of what each costs. This is the missing content for the CP2 path-picker panel.
adapt.whatMustChange: **Drop every conversion factor.** `TIME_CONVERSION_FACTOR = 0.12` (pressure cooker) and `2.5` (sous-vide) are uncited invented numbers that would *generate cook durations* — the one thing our engine has never done. Keep the vector, make it a small cited enum per path (`bark`, `smokeRing`, `juiciness`, `pink`) stored in `sources.py` alongside `order_svsmoke`/`order_smokesv`, which already carry a per-path `note`. And drop the pressure-cooker/braise conversion entirely until those methods exist in `methodRules().allowed` (today: `sv|smoke|grill` only).

adapt.item: Consumables calculator (§6.4) — fuel/paper quantities with a safety buffer.
adapt.why: A genuine gap, already logged: gap D4 *"equipPlan seam narrow; cook stages carry no equipment-specific instruction"* and D10 are OPEN in the BIG-STATUS doc. `equipPlan()` (app.js:1146) sets only `fuelNote` and `refuelEveryMin` — it tells you *when* to reload, never *how much to buy*. The shopping-list surface exists (app.js:10049 inventory groups).
adapt.whatMustChange: The rates (`~1.5 ק"ג גזעי עץ/שעה` offset, `0.8` cabinet, `1.0/2.0` pellet, `1.5m` paper per wrapped cut) are stated with no source. Either cite them or ship them as an **explicitly-labelled estimate** with a range, never as a flat number — we already have the honest-estimate pattern for area (`FIT_HARD_FACTOR = 1.6` loosens the verdict when the number is derived rather than measured, app.js:347). Reuse `REFUEL_MIN`/`DEVICE_FUEL` as the per-device-type keying rather than inventing a parallel smoker taxonomy.

adapt.item: Smoke-intensity multiplier per smoker type (§4.3: offset 1.5 / charcoal cabinet 1.2 / pellet 0.8 / electric-gas 0.6).
adapt.why: Real and true directionally — an offset burning splits delivers far more smoke than a pellet grill, and our per-recipe `wood` field plus the v267 wood advisory does not model it. It would let the wood advisory say "on a pellet, go one step stronger" instead of repeating the recipe's wood.
adapt.whatMustChange: The four coefficients are uncited and dimensionless — they multiply nothing defined. Ship it as an **ordinal** (`strong | medium | mild`) driving advisory prose, not a scalar multiplying any temperature or duration. Under DoD-10 it must be provably incapable of altering a `bcheck` stage, a `temp`, a `safe` value, or a cook duration.

adapt.item: Cloudflare Worker + Supabase tier — but scoped to **user/event data and IoT ingestion only**, never the rules engine and never the safety values.
adapt.why: §6.1's point is sound and is the one thing a PWA structurally cannot do: a webhook from Meater/Inkbird/ThermoWorks needs a server endpoint to receive the push. Same for multi-device event sync and push notifications. Our existing Worker (`worker/index.js`, 91 lines) is a thin Gemini proxy with a KV code store — it has no persistence and no logic; the shape v5.0 describes is the honest extension of it.
adapt.whatMustChange: **Two hard exclusions.** (a) The rules engine must NOT move to the Worker. `eqmValidity` runs on the catalog's per-keystroke debounced re-render across ~279 cards — the codebase carries an explicit performance comment about exactly this (app.js:254: *"eqmValidity/eqInvState ran 3-4 uncached ownership computations PER CARD on the catalog grid's per-keystroke re-render path"*), which is why `_eqValidityCache` and `_eqDefReqCache` are generation-stamped. A network round-trip per card per keystroke is not a viable architecture. (b) Safety values must NOT become table rows — see the reject entry on §9.1. Also: any prose the server generates bypasses `L()` and therefore Guard A/B/C — server output must be **codes and numbers only**, rendered through the client dictionary.

adapt.item: Telemetry-driven stall detection and device-failure reroute (§5.5, §6.3, `RealTimeCulinaryEngine`).
adapt.why: Overlaps our approved Phase 3a solver (`share → wood-swap → reassign → cook-early-and-hold → advise`) but adds two moves we do not have: detect a stall and act, and fall back when a device dies mid-cook. The `cooler` token (`צידנית / קמברו (החזקה חמה)`) is already in our equipment vocabulary and already derived onto 13 cuts — the Faux Cambro buffer is a data field we own and do not yet use.
adapt.whatMustChange: v5.0 lets telemetry *drive* actions (`Stall 69-73°C → WRAP`, `CRISIS_SPEED_UP → +15°C chamber`). Our Phase 3a spec §5.1 rules the opposite way and for a good reason: *"User telemetry is not a vetted source"* — it documents a **shipped bug** where `copilotVoiceContext()` injected the live probe reading into `aiSafetyNote`'s grounding, so any number the user's own thermometer reported counted as vetted. Any telemetry engine must land on the safe side of that line: telemetry may *inform* a proposal, may never *ground* a safety number, and every emitted move must pass `safetyGate` (hold floor 60°C, danger-zone budget ≤240 min, `holdCapMin` 360 min, poultry/fish never holdable).

reject.item: §4.1 Rule 4 — `IF PROTEIN == "Fish" AND P_TARGET_INT > 60°C -> SET P_TARGET_INT = 52°C AND NOTIFY_USER("Adjusted to prevent fish from drying out")`
reject.defect: It silently **rewrites a cited target temperature** and then tells the user it did so, in an authoritative voice. It is also factually wrong for a whole class of seafood we ship.
reject.evidence: Our cut #123 Octopus is `svt 77 / tgt 75`, citing ChefSteps and Thomas Keller *Under Pressure* (77°C/5h) — octopus is cooked hot and long precisely to convert collagen. Cut #124 Squid is `svt 59 / tgt 63` (amazingfoodmadeeasy, 138°F/59°C for 2–3h). Rule 4 would drive both to 52°C and produce rubber, while announcing the change as a correction. Separately, DoD-10 forbids altering any `temp`, `safe`, or cook duration; a rule whose entire body is `SET P_TARGET_INT` cannot pass that gate.

reject.item: §3.3 cuts table, liver row: `כבד | GRILL | 220°C | טמפ' יעד 63-65°C`
reject.defect: Below the USDA organ-meat floor our own data cites. This is the clearest safety defect in the proposal.
reject.evidence: Our cut #72 Beef Liver: `tgt 72 / safe 72`, citing `https://ask.usda.gov/s/article/What-is-the-safe-temperature-to-cook-organ-meat` — *"USDA organ meat 160°F… 72°C keeps it above 71°C organ floor."* #73 Lamb Liver identical. #71 Chicken Liver: `tgt 74 / safe 74`, citing USDA + Baldwin — *"chicken liver carries salmonella/campylobacter risk → cook to 74°C/165°F throughout."* v5.0's 63–65°C is below both floors, and the table does not distinguish poultry liver from beef liver.

reject.item: §4.1 Rule 5 — `IF CATEGORY == "Cheese" AND P_COOK_METHOD == "SMOKE": IF P_CHAMBER_TEMP > 30°C: RETURN ERROR`
reject.defect: Hard-blocks two real, shipped, cited items. A false block is worse than no rule — it makes the engine untrustworthy on exactly the items where it speaks most loudly.
reject.evidence: `SPECIALS` #19 גבינת שמנת מעושנת / Smoked Cream Cheese ships at `smt: 110` °C — the note says *"טרנד BBQ — מעשנים חם עם ראב"*. #47 חלומי / Halloumi is a grilling cheese by definition. Our data already encodes the cold-smoke case correctly and per-item: #39 Blue Cheese is `smt: 28`. The right mechanism is a per-recipe cited number (which we have), not a category-wide 30°C ceiling.

reject.item: §4.5 `generateRecipePipeline`'s `throw new Error` control flow (5 throw sites, incl. equipment gaps and bath volume).
reject.defect: An exception is a dead end. Our three-level verdict explains and offers remedies, and never blocks an item that has a working alternative.
reject.evidence: `eqmValidity` returns `{level, okPaths, gaps, fixes}`; `level` is `'blocked-default'` when `okPaths.length` (app.js:1914), and `eqmAddGate` blocks only on `'uncookable'` (app.js:2063). `fixes` is built deterministically in order of cheapness (app.js:1941–1947): configure equipment → *"זמין במסלול: <path>"* per working cited path → the E5 replacement placeholder. We even ship `eqmValidityWithKit` (app.js:2151), an injectable-kit what-if that answers "would buying a probe unlock anything?" without mutating the registry, plus `eqmRetroImpact` for the delete-a-device case with a real N/M count. v5.0's throw discards all of it.

reject.item: §9.1 — *"עדכון גלובלי (טמפ' בטיחות עוף 74°C→73°C) = שורה אחת"* (a global safety-temperature change is one Postgres row).
reject.defect: Directly incompatible with the non-negotiable citation rule, and it removes every gate that today stands between a safety number and production.
reject.evidence: CLAUDE.md and `docs/sources/baldwin-backbone.md`: *every `safe` value must trace to a cited primary source — never guess*. Today a safety value lives in `data.py`, is merged with its citation from `sources.py` (130 `CUT_SOURCES` + 47 `SPEC_SOURCES` + 102 `MAKE_SOURCES`) at build time, and any change passes `build.py`'s Guard B (unit-class preservation: *"חילוף g↔kg או °C↔°F נכשל בבנייה"*) plus DoD-10 plus the 816-test suite. A mutable server row has none of that. Cite-and-build is the feature, not the friction. (For *user* data — devices, events, live timeline — Supabase is fine.)

reject.item: §4.1 Rule 3 / §4.2 sugar threshold `P_CHAMBER_TEMP > 140°C` — contradicted by §7's `ללא סוכר מעל 120°C`.
reject.defect: The same document gives two different thresholds for the same phenomenon, and the higher one would never fire on our actual smoke temperatures. Our unconditional rule is strictly safer.
reject.evidence: Two numbers, one document: §4.1 Rule 3 and §4.2 both say `> 140°C`; §7 says *"ללא סוכר מעל 120°C"*. Our smoke temps are 105–120°C for the collagen cuts (brisket `smt 105 / sot 110`), so the 140°C rule generates **no** delay on an 8–12h brisket smoke — sugar sits on the meat for the whole cook. `injectSeasoningSteps` (app.js:1288) already places every glaze *"ב-10-15 הדקות האחרונות של הבישול, בשכבות"* unconditionally, and template line 1616 says *"מרח גלייז דביק ב-30 הדקות האחרונות"*. Adopting v5.0's conditional here would be a behavioural **loosening**. The disagreement between §4.1 and §7 is itself the tell that these numbers are not sourced.

reject.item: §5.2 `EventOptimizationEngine.optimizeEvent` — spatial allocation performed independently of, and before, the schedule.
reject.defect: It packs every menu item onto shelves as if all were resident simultaneously for the whole event, then throws `חסימת נפח` on schedules that are trivially feasible in time. It also never bounds hanging capacity.
reject.evidence: The code allocates in one pass over `menu` (`for (let item of menu) { … if (!allocated) throw … }`) and only afterwards computes `cookStartTime`/`cookEndTime` per item. Its own worked example — *asado enters 11:00, chicken 17:45* — has the two items overlapping for barely an hour, yet both consume shelf area for the entire run. Our `cookerContention` (app.js:307) evaluates `deviceOccupancy(devId, tMs, computed, scope)` **at every instant a device's load could change**, and judges by the honest per-slot verdict rather than a whole-device area sum — the comment at app.js:323 records that we already fixed exactly the lie the naive sum produces. Second defect: `if (placement_preference === "HANGING" && supports_hanging) { hangingUsed++; allocated = true; }` — `hangingUsed` is incremented and never compared to anything, so hook capacity is infinite. We carry `cap.hooks` and a derived `hang` class (`short`/`long`) per recipe. Third: `scheduleTimeline.sort((a,b) => a.action_start_entry.localeCompare(b.action_start_entry))` sorts formatted `HH:MM` strings, which breaks across midnight — an overnight brisket is the single most common case in this product.

reject.item: §5.2 `action_wrap_stall = cookStartTime + (required_cook_time_mins * 0.6)` — the stall as a fixed 60% of elapsed cook time.
reject.defect: The stall is an evaporative-cooling plateau at an *internal temperature*, not a fraction of the clock. Modelling it as a time fraction is wrong in the one direction that matters — a stall that comes early on a windy day leaves the user with no wrap instruction.
reject.evidence: v5.0's own §3.3 says the opposite in the same document: *"חובה לעטוף ב-71°C (The Stall)"* — a temperature. This is precisely why the `advanceWhen: {tempC}` predicate (my ADOPT item 1) is the right mechanism and this formula is not. Note also that we currently model wrap barely at all: `wrap` is `'לא'` for **127 of 130** cuts, because our default path is sv→smoke where sous-vide does the collagen work. The wrap decision is a genuine gap on the smoke-only path (`sot`/`soh`, e.g. brisket 110°C/12h) — but the fix is a cited per-recipe wrap trigger, not a 0.6 multiplier.

reject.defect: Conflates the wrap point with the finish target, and applies a single number across every non-beef protein including fish.
reject.evidence: Our brisket is `tgt 95` (AmazingRibs: *"magical around 203F (95C)"*). A brisket smoked to 71°C and served is safe but inedible. For fish the same line yields 74°C — which contradicts the document's own Rule 4 (fish → 52°C) and its own §3.3 salmon row (50–52°C), and would wreck our #49 Salmon (`svt 50 / tgt 52`, Baldwin 43–50°C). Three parts of one document give three different numbers for the same field.

reject.item: Running the rules engine inside a Cloudflare Worker (§9.2: *"Cloudflare Worker = מנוע החוקים v5.0"*).
reject.defect: It converts our hottest synchronous read path into a network round trip.
reject.evidence: `eqmValidity` is called from `eqInvState` for every catalog card, on the debounced per-keystroke re-render across ~279 cards. app.js:254 documents this explicitly, and both `_eqValidityCache` and `_eqDefReqCache` exist as generation-stamped caches solely to survive it. Same for `itemStages`, which every surface reads (card stat/steps/raw-table, catalog grid row, work-plan detail, AI grounding — the four CP1 unified). Server-side rules would also route engine prose around `L()`, re-opening the v274–v277 render-leak class that took four releases to close, at a layer Guard A/B/C cannot inspect.

impactOnUs:
**If we adopt only my ADOPT + ADAPT list (recommended):**

- `app.js` `itemStages()` (lines 4093–4169) — gains an optional `advanceWhen` field on stage objects. This is the single stage authority CP1 established; every consumer (`deriveRequires`, `planSchedule`, `eqmValidity` via `itemPaths`, the work-plan stage renderer at 7421, the AI grounding) inherits it for free. Absent field = today's behaviour exactly, so the 816-test suite is unaffected by construction.
- `app.js` `methodRules()` / `validCombo()` (989–1048) — read the cited `grillable` flag. Narrows `itemPaths` output for 25 cuts; `eqmValidity.okPaths` shrinks correspondingly, which can flip a small number of items from `blocked-default` to `uncookable`. **This is a real behaviour change and needs its own RED/GREEN plus a rendered-DOM check per DoD-4/8.**
- `app.js` `itemPaths()` (4175–4189) — `cited:true` becomes conditional rather than a literal, and each path gains a small cited `effects` vector (bark / smokeRing / juiciness / pink). This is CP2 input; it belongs in the CP2 path-picker panel, not a separate feature.
- `sources.py` — new per-path keys alongside the existing `order_svsmoke` / `order_smokesv` objects: the `effects` enum and any `advanceWhen` trigger temperature. **A 130-cut research pass with citations** — the largest single cost, and the part that cannot be delegated to an engine.
- `app.js` `equipPlan()` (1146–1159) + `DEVICE_FUEL` / `REFUEL_MIN` — gains a consumables quantity alongside the existing `fuelNote` / `refuelEveryMin`. Feeds the existing inventory groups (app.js:10049, `'מלח וסוכר'` / `'תבלינים'` …). Closes gap D4/D10 partially.
- `equipment_map.py` — no schema change needed; `paper`, `foil`, `cooler`, `torch`, `spritz`, `chimney`, `gloves` are already in `VOCAB` and already derived onto recipes (brisket's smoke block already lists `opt: [drippan, spritz, gloves, paper, foil, cooler]`).
- `equipment.js` `deriveRequires()` (63–116) — the O-7 probe rule generalises: any stage carrying a `tempC` predicate implies `capability.probe`, not just the terminal `bcheck`.
- `lang/*.json` + `build.py` Guards A/B/C — every new string goes through `L()` with static literals. Guard A currently enforces 1535 keys × 6 languages; each new label adds 6 required translations. The effects-vector labels and consumables units are the visible additions.
- **Untouched:** `data.py` cut records, every `safe` value, every `tgt`, every cook duration, `sources.py` citation bodies, `worker/index.js`.

**If we adopted v5.0 wholesale (not recommended):** `data.py`'s 116 distinct cited schedules collapse to ~4 engine constants; `sources.py`'s 279 citations lose their referents; `eqmValidity`'s three-level verdict + `fixes` + `eqmValidityWithKit` + `eqmRetroImpact` are replaced by five `throw` sites; `methodRules`/`validCombo`/`itemProfile`/`comboMethodEntry` are replaced by a less capable enumerator that cannot express smoke+sv in one pipeline; and the safety layer moves from build-time-guarded constants to mutable rows. The 816-test suite would not survive, and neither would DoD-10.

risks.risk: Adopting any v5.0 number as-is. The proposal asserts ~40 numeric values (chamber temps, target temps, conversion factors 0.12/2.5, smoke multipliers 1.5/1.2/0.8/0.6, consumption rates, the 0.6 stall fraction, weight_kg*3 bath volume) and cites **zero** sources. At least three of them contradict our cited data or the proposal's own other sections.
risks.mitigation: Treat the document as a **mechanism catalogue, not a data source**. Adopt shapes; re-derive every number from a primary source or ship it as an explicitly-labelled ordinal/range. Enforce mechanically: any task touching a `safe`/`temp`/duration must quote its citation in the DoD-1 line, and DoD-10 must be checked against a named assertion.

risks.risk: The `advanceWhen` stage field touches `itemStages` — CP1's single stage authority, read by the item card, the catalog row, the work-plan detail, and the AI grounding. CP1 closed precisely because those four had diverged.
risks.mitigation: Ship it strictly additive with an absent-field default that reproduces today's output byte-for-byte, and add a characterization test asserting that every existing stage array is unchanged before adding a single predicate. Verify all four surfaces in the rendered DOM (DoD-4/8), not by assertion alone — this is exactly the L8 'named render path that never fires' failure shape.

risks.risk: The `grillable` fix changes real verdicts: some items will move from `blocked-default` to `uncookable`, which changes catalog emphasis AND blocks `eqmAddGate`. A user who could add an item yesterday cannot today.
risks.mitigation: Compute the impact set first (the same `eqmRetroImpact` N/M machinery already answers 'how many items flip' without shipping anything), show the owner the list, and get an explicit decision before building. If the count is large, the honest alternative is to surface the citation's objection as an advisory on the path rather than removing the path.

risks.risk: Server-side scope creep: a Supabase tier introduced for IoT telemetry drifts into holding the catalog, then the safety values, because 'it's all one database anyway'. §9.1 explicitly argues for that drift.
risks.mitigation: Write the boundary into the spec before any schema exists: the server stores **user state only** (fleet, events, live_timeline, telemetry samples). The catalog, the citations, and every `safe`/`tgt`/duration remain build-time constants in the shipped bundle, verified by Guards A/B/C. No server table may contain a temperature that is not a user reading. Add a build-time check that fails if it does.

risks.risk: Server-generated prose bypasses `L()` and therefore Guard A (coverage), Guard B (numeric/unit preservation), and Guard C (translator garbage). v274–v277 took four releases to close this exact leak class in client code.
risks.mitigation: Contract: the server returns **codes and numbers only** — `{action_id, kind, tempC, minutes}` — never a rendered sentence. All wording is built client-side through `L()` with static literals. This is the same discipline the approved Phase 3a `action_id` contract already imposes on the AI.

risks.risk: Opportunity cost. CP2 is approved and waiting on an owner decision (11 tasks, 150 code blocks); the roadmap behind it is E4 → CP3 → CP4 → E5/E6 → orchestrator P8. The 141-gap charter shows P4/P5/P7/P8 not started. Anything from v5.0 that is not folded into CP2 or P8 displaces built work by design.
risks.mitigation: Fold — do not append. The path effects-vector and the cited-`grillable` fix are CP2 tasks. Telemetry/stall/reroute is a Phase 3b task. Consumables is a D4/D10 task in P5a. Only the Worker/Supabase tier is genuinely new scope, and it should be a separate arc with its own spec and owner approval, not a rider on CP2.

risks.risk: Adopting the proposal's framing wholesale would re-open our own settled architecture questions with an outside document as the authority. Under the Waiver Gate (§4), several v5.0 mechanisms would silently narrow approved-spec requirements — e.g. `throw`-on-blocked reinterprets E3's O-5 three-level honesty ladder, and telemetry-driven actions reinterpret Phase 3a §5.1's telemetry-is-not-vetted ruling.
risks.mitigation: Any v5.0 mechanism that touches an approved spec (E3's O-5 levels, Phase 3a §3.5 safety floors, Phase 3a §4.1 action_id, CP1's single stage authority) goes to the owner in conversation with both texts quoted, before any plan is written. Recording it in a document does not count.

costEstimate:
**On the engine-architecture lens only, and assuming the recommended narrow adoption:**

- `grillable` cited-flag fix in `methodRules`/`validCombo`/`itemPaths` — **small**, roughly one task. Code is ~5 lines; the work is the impact analysis and the rendered verification across the catalog grid + item panel + add gate.
- Path effects-vector (gain/loss per cited path) — **small-medium**, and it should be absorbed into CP2 rather than costed separately. The code is trivial; the research pass to attach a cited effects enum to ~250 path entries is the real work.
- `advanceWhen` stage predicate — **medium**, the biggest genuine engine change. Roughly: 1 task for the field + defaults + characterization, 1 for `deriveRequires`/probe generalization, 1 for the work-plan and item-card render, 1 for the Playwright coverage. Plus a **130-cut cited research pass** for the trigger temperatures — that is the dominant cost and it is unavoidable under the citation rule. Realistically several days of focused research work, not an afternoon.
- Consumables quantities — **medium**, gated entirely on sourcing burn rates. If no citable source exists, ship as a labelled range and the code cost drops to small.
- Smoke-intensity ordinal — **small**, advisory prose only.
- Worker/Supabase tier for sync + telemetry ingestion — **large**, and a different kind of large: schema, RLS, auth, migrations, a second deploy target, secret handling, offline reconciliation, and a whole new test surface (our 816 tests are Playwright against a single-file build; none of them exercise a server). This is an arc, not a task.

**What it displaces:** the current sequence is CP2 (approved, 11 tasks, awaiting owner go) → E4 → CP3 → CP4 → E5/E6 → orchestrator P8, against a 141-gap charter with P4/P5/P7/P8 not started. The narrow adoption costs roughly **one CP-sized unit** if folded into CP2 and P5a, and displaces almost nothing because it lands inside work already planned. The Worker/Supabase arc displaces **at least E4 through E6** and would push the orchestrator further out. My recommendation on this lens: take the engine items now inside CP2/P5a; make the infrastructure tier a separate decision driven by whether IoT telemetry and multi-device sync are actually product goals — not by this document's architecture diagram.
openQuestions: **Provenance and sourcing.** Who or what produced this document, and can that source supply primary citations for its ~40 asserted numbers? The internal contradictions I found (sugar threshold 140°C in §4.1/§4.2 vs 120°C in §7; fish target 52°C in Rule 4 vs 50–52°C in §3.3 vs 74°C in the §4.5 code; §4.5's engine unable to produce §3.2's own flagship pipeline) read as generated-not-derived. If no sources are forthcoming, the numeric layer is unusable for us and only the mechanism shapes survive — which is what I have recommended. Owner call on whether to go back and ask.

**Is server-side state actually a product goal now?** The infrastructure verdict hinges entirely on this. If the driver is IoT thermometer ingestion, a Worker endpoint plus a small store is the answer and Supabase may be more than we need. If the driver is multi-device sync, auth, and shared events, Supabase is right-sized. If neither is a near-term goal, the whole §9 section is premature and the answer is 'not yet'. Only you can say which.

**`grillable`: should the cited flag gate combo enumeration?** We ship a per-cut boolean in `sources.py` with its own `src.grill` citation (25 cuts are `False`), and `methodRules()` ignores it in favour of a category heuristic. Making it authoritative is a one-line change with real user-visible consequences — some items will become un-addable. Do you want the citation to win, or the heuristic?

**Do we want to model the wrap/crutch stage at all?** `wrap` is `'לא'` for 127 of 130 cuts, because our default sv→smoke path makes the Texas Crutch unnecessary. But the smoke-only path (`sot`/`soh` — brisket 110°C for 12h) is a real path we ship, and on it the wrap decision (none / butcher paper / foil, each with a different bark-and-moisture outcome per §2.1) is one of the biggest choices a pitmaster makes. This would be new cited data for ~30 collagen cuts. In scope, or deliberately out?

**Where does `advanceWhen` belong — CP2 or Phase 3b?** As a *path property* it is CP2 (the path picker shows what triggers each transition). As a *live-cook mechanism* it is Phase 3b (the Copilot compares a probe reading against the predicate and advances the stage). Building it in CP2 delivers less but unblocks 3b; building it in 3b means CP2 ships without it. Your sequencing call.

**Do you want the proposal's method vocabulary extended?** `methodRules().allowed` is `['sv','smoke','grill']` today. v5.0 adds `OVEN_BRAISE`, `PRESSURE_COOKER`, `COLD_SMOKE`, `PAN_SEAR`. `oven` is already an equipment token in `VOCAB` and appears as an `alt` in derived equip blocks, and CP3 already has oven-only / sv→oven reserved as path placeholders. Braise and pressure-cooking would be genuinely new domains with their own citation burden. Is expanding the method space a goal, or is the current three the deliberate scope?
